assumptions.statement: Portable archive normalization and explicit interpreters remain valid on independent ZIP extractors and operating systems.
Persistent replay semantics remain correct on shared durable storage and multiple hosts.
Bounded telemetry and evidence-bound action lifecycle reduce operator error and review time.
Local throughput gains remain directionally useful on other developer hosts.
Explicit internal registry allowlisting is sufficient only when the mirror itself is governed and independently reviewed.
A fixture-backed governed model validates orchestration contracts but does not predict network inference latency, model quality or provider availability.
Proposal-only engineering assistance improves operator outcomes only if confirmed by a consented human comparison pilot.
Repository-local architecture closure remains valid on independent operating systems and multi-host runtime topology.
The declared in-process coverage scope is representative of branch logic while subprocess and host-isolation paths remain separately exercised by correctness lanes.
Historical source capability maps accurately identify useful behavior, but do not replace re-execution of current source archives.
The ingestion boundary verifies evidence signatures against an independently governed trust store before setting signature.verified=true.
Pilot and SLO thresholds are preregistered before external execution and are not altered after outcomes are observed.
Static operator task-flow reduction is directionally useful for pilot design but is not human outcome evidence.
Repository-local independent oracles reduce correlated test risk but do not establish legal or organizational independence.
Official repository ownership and signed releases reduce intake risk but do not substitute for executing Scorecard, signature, policy, formal or fuzz qualification on the exact revision.
Local Dapr-envelope conformance predicts contract portability but does not prove actual Dapr runtime or external daemon behavior.
Dapr SPIRE OpenTelemetry and CloudNativePG external runtimes will conform to the locally validated portable contracts only after pinned-version qualification.
Distinct local Node processes and loopback HTTP demonstrate process isolation and network retrieval but not external host or organization independence.
